summary: Studies strongly motivate independent measurement and layered evidence. They do not validate one universal trust score; trust remains task-, environment- and consequence-specific.

items.text: METR's randomized trial with experienced open-source developers found that early-2025 AI tools made participants 19% slower on the studied tasks even though participants expected acceleration, illustrating why perceived productivity must be checked against measured outcomes; the setting and tool generation are narrow.
DORA's 2025 research reports that AI tends to amplify an organization's existing strengths and weaknesses, supporting a systems-level trust layer rather than tool adoption metrics alone.
Can LLMs Replace Human Evaluators? (TOSEM 2025) examines agreement and reliability limits of LLM-as-judge methods, warning against treating automated evaluators as ground truth.
NIST AI RMF 1.0 (2023) provides governance guidance for valid and reliable measurement, transparency and risk management; it is a framework, not an effectiveness experiment.
